 BUA Cement Declares N463bn PAT in 9M 2026 Unaudited Results; (SP: N293.4)
 Oct 29, 2026   •   
 by Proshare Data and Content   •   
 Source: NGX Group   •   
 263 views 
 Share 
   Facebook 
   X 
   Whatsapp 
   LinkedIn 
   Google 
   Yahoo 
 BUA Cement Plc’s nine-month 2026 results show stronger earnings resilience, with revenue up 26.5% to N1.10trn and profit after tax up 59.8% to N463.10bn. Profit before tax advanced 64.43% to N556.71bn, while gross profit and EBITDA margins expanded to 57.1% and 52.7%, respectively.  
 Investors should monitor sales volumes, energy costs, logistics efficiency, and margin sustainability at the reported share price of N293.40 to assess whether current earnings momentum can be sustained. 
 BUA Cement Plc   released its unaudited financial statements for the nine months ended September 2026, reflecting three consecutive quarters of volume growth compared with the corresponding periods in 2025, despite heavy rainfall and poor road conditions. The performance also highlights the Company’s continued focus on operational and financial efficiencies. 
 Despite last quarter's challenges, revenue grew 26.5% to N1.1trn in 9M 2026, from N858.7bn in 9M 2025, supported by continued growth in bulk cement sales. Cost of sales rose by 8.8% to N466.4bn, from N428.6bn, partly due to an adverse energy mix, operational challenges, and elevated prices linked to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Even so, gross profit and EBITDA margins improved by 7.0 and 6.3 percentage points, to 57.1% and 52.7%, respectively. Lower O&M service charges and cost savings from introducing LNG-powered trucks supported these gains. 
 Return on Equity and Asset stood at 63% and 27.4%, respectively, reflecting further improvements in operating margin, asset turnover, and interest burden. 
 Key Highlights  
 Revenue grows by 26.5% to N1.10trn from N858.73bn in 9M 2025.  
  Profit before tax rises by 64.43% to N556.71bn from N338.56bn in 9M 2025.  
 Profit after tax rose by 59.8% to N463.10bn in 9M 2026, from N289.85bn in 9M 2025. 
 Share Price currently stands at N293.40 
 Speaking on the results, the Managing Director/CEO, Yusuf Binji said:   I am delighted with our performance, which demonstrates resilience despite challenging conditions, particularly on account of the heavy rainfall and its impact on road infrastructure. We surpassed our quarterly performance in 2025 through the addition of bulk customers, the acquisition of LNG trucks, and the further restructuring of our logistics operations.  
 The LNG trucks are eco-friendly, thus reducing our carbon footprint on the environment while harnessing the country’s abundant gas reserves. This investment will also enhance market penetration and operational efficiency. Energy costs were elevated during the quarter due to supply constraints but have since normalised.    
 Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we remain committed to achieving our objectives through profitable partnerships with our distributors and sustained efforts to reduce our cost to serve.
